name: App and device identifiers
plain: IDs the OS gives an app to recognize an install or a vendor's apps.
meaning: Lets a company recognize the same install across sessions and link sessions without login. Some survive reinstall (iOS Keychain, backups).

android.persistence: ANDROID_ID per app signing key; resets on factory reset

ios.persistence: IDFV persists across apps of one vendor; resets when all vendor apps are removed

limits.headline: Can use IDs your phone gives it to recognize this install or the developer's apps
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app can get them as soon as it opens
can: Use Android ID to recognize you across the same developer's apps
Use the iPhone vendor ID to recognize you across the same developer's apps
Use a Firebase install ID to tell one install from another
Save an ID in the iPhone Keychain so it can stay after a reinstall
cannot: Match you across different developers with these IDs
Show your name or phone number
Stay the same after a factory reset on Android
Be turned off with a prompt; the person can only reset or delete apps
limits.differs: Android ID and iPhone vendor ID work the same way but have different reset rules.

story.what_it_is: IDs the phone gives an app so it can recognize an install or a company's apps.

marketing.name: User data IDs
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: Android's guidance on which IDs to use, which reset, and which need consent.

marketing.name: identifierForVendor
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: an ID shared by one vendor's apps on a device, reset when they are all deleted.

story.for_you: You never see them. They quietly let an app know it is the same phone as yesterday. Some reset when you reinstall, some are shared across one company's apps, and some are hidden if you refuse tracking.
story.for_makers: Makers need an ID to save progress, count users and fight fraud. Ad firms want a stable ID to link activity. The phone makers now limit which IDs apps can read and when.

use_cases.example: A game saves your progress against an install ID so a quick restart does not lose your level.
An ad network counts how many different phones saw an ad, so one person is not counted ten times.
A product team counts daily users and joins crash logs to one install without asking for a login.
A bank links a new login to a device ID it has seen before and skips extra checks.
A store gives a welcome coupon once per install ID.
A chat app uses an install ID as the address for push notifications.

story.android_note: Includes the resettable ad ID, the per signing key Android ID and app set IDs.
story.ios_note: Includes the vendor ID and the ad ID, which needs your tracking permission.

technical_bounds: Hardware IDs are not available to normal apps

UDID and MAC address blocked; IDFV introduced
